scenes.text: This Sunday, Europe gets one extra hour of sleep, and it all started with a war.
On October twenty fifth, clocks across Europe go back one hour. America does it a week later.
In nineteen sixteen, Germany became the first country to use daylight saving time nationwide.
The goal was to save fuel during World War One.
Benjamin Franklin once joked about it too, telling Parisians to wake up earlier to save candles.
Should we keep changing the clocks, or stop for good?

title: Why the clocks go back this weekend ⏰
caption: Clocks in Europe go back 1 hour on Sunday, October 25 (US: November 1). Germany was the first country to adopt daylight saving time nationwide in 1916, to save fuel in WWI. ⏰
